scope: Assigned application/platform chapters; infrastructure chapters mapped by infrastructure agent

scenarios.title: Role based access control
scenarios.stepTitle: Give a release bot limited access
scenarios.task: In `book-cka-rbac`, create `release-bot`, Role `release-manager` and its RoleBinding. Allow get/list/watch/update/patch Deployments and get/list/watch ConfigMaps. Deny Secret access, Deployment create/delete and permissions in other namespaces.

scenarios.title: Role based access control
scenarios.stepTitle: Bind reusable rules within one namespace
scenarios.task: Create ServiceAccounts `demo-sa` and `demo2-sa` in `book-cka-rbac`. Create ClusterRole `book-cka-creators` permitting creation of Deployments and DaemonSets and bind it to `demo-sa` only in this namespace. Let `demo2-sa` create only Deployments. Neither account may read Secrets or create objects in `default`.

scenarios.title: Pod with a specific ServiceAccount
scenarios.stepTitle: Run a Pod without an API token
scenarios.task: Create Ready Pod `web-identity` with image `nginx:1.28.0` and ServiceAccount `demo-sa` in `book-cka-rbac`. Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false`. The web container must have no API token file or projected service-account-token volume.

scenarios.title: Troubleshoot Services and CoreDNS
scenarios.stepTitle: Repair the Service and client resolver
scenarios.task: In `book-cka-service`, restore HTTP from `client` to `web.book-cka-service.svc.cluster.local`. Repair the selector, target port and client DNS configuration. Keep the existing web Deployment. Save a short diagnosis naming each fault to `~/book-labs/cka-02-service-repair/causes.txt`.

scenarios.title: Troubleshoot a broken application from events to endpoints
scenarios.stepTitle: Recover a workload through events and endpoints
scenarios.task: In `book-cka-incident`, restore two available replicas of `web` and HTTP through its Service. Fix the unavailable image to `nginx:1.28.0`, ConfigMap reference to `app-config`, requests to 100m CPU/64Mi memory, limit to 128Mi memory, and Service targetPort to named port `http`. Create a test Pod `client`. Save four causes and observed recovery to `~/book-labs/cka-02-service-repair/incident.txt`.

scenarios.title: Apply a Kustomize overlay
scenarios.stepTitle: Render and apply an application overlay
scenarios.task: Use the prepared app/base in your lab work directory. Keep the prepared base unchanged. Create app/overlays/prod: prefix prod-, three replicas, nginx:1.28.0, and environment=production labels on workload and Service selectors. Save app/rendered.yaml, apply the overlay, and prove the Service reaches the application.

scenarios.title: Apply a Kustomize overlay
scenarios.stepTitle: Patch and install a real metrics component
scenarios.task: The prepared metrics/base contains the pinned official Metrics Server v0.8.1 manifests and a public trust bundle for this VM’s real kubelet serving certificate. Create metrics/overlay that changes only the metrics-server CPU request to 200m. Save metrics/rendered.yaml, apply it, and obtain live metrics. Keep kubelet certificate verification enabled.

scenarios.title: Static local PV and reclaim policy
scenarios.stepTitle: Bind a genuine static local volume
scenarios.task: On the node named in node.txt, setup created /var/book-labs/cka-local/data containing marker.txt. Create StorageClass book-cka-local (no provisioner, WaitForFirstConsumer), PV book-cka-local-data (local path, node affinity, 1Gi, RWO, Retain), PVC data and a BusyBox reader in book-cka-storage. Read the existing marker from the mounted claim. Use a local PV, not a hostPath PV.

scenarios.title: Static local PV and reclaim policy
scenarios.stepTitle: Observe Retain after deleting a claim
scenarios.task: Create a second local PV book-cka-local-retained for /var/book-labs/cka-local/retained (same class, capacity, access mode and Retain). Bind PVC retained using Pod writer, write retained-after-claim-deletion to retained.txt, save the PVC UID to deleted-claim-uid.txt, then delete writer and its PVC. Leave the PV Released and its data intact. Keep the first exercise running.

scenarios.title: Labels and node selectors
scenarios.stepTitle: Repair a node selector
scenarios.task: Label the worker listed in node.txt with book-labs.example/disk=ssd. Recreate `reporter` in `book-cka-scheduling` using `busybox:1.37.0`, requiring `book-labs.example/disk=ssd`. Keep it running. Let the scheduler select the node; do not set nodeName.

scenarios.title: Assign a Pod directly to a node
scenarios.stepTitle: Assign a Pod directly to a node
scenarios.task: Create `direct` in `book-cka-scheduling` using `nginx:1.28.0`, with explicit `spec.nodeName` equal to the node listed in `~/book-labs/cka-05-scheduling/node.txt`. Save its submitted manifest as `direct.yaml` in that directory. This task deliberately bypasses scheduling.

scenarios.title: Scheduling with Pod affinity
scenarios.stepTitle: Co-locate using required Pod affinity
scenarios.task: Create Ready Pod anchor using nginx:1.28.0 and label role=anchor. Create Ready Pod `near-anchor` in `book-cka-scheduling`, image `redis:7.4.5`, with required Pod affinity to `role=anchor` on topology key `kubernetes.io/hostname`. Do not set nodeName or a nodeSelector. Keep the anchor Pod.

scenarios.title: DaemonSet
scenarios.stepTitle: Run a DaemonSet on every node
scenarios.task: Create DaemonSet `node-web` in `book-cka-scheduling` with image `nginx:1.28.0`. Run one Ready Pod per Ready node, including a control-plane node with its normal NoSchedule taint. Do not use replicas to emulate the result.

scenarios.title: Create a Deployment
scenarios.stepTitle: Create and inspect a Deployment
scenarios.task: Create Deployment `created` in `book-cka-rollout` with three replicas of `nginx:1.28.0`. Save its live YAML as `~/book-labs/cka-06-rollout-recovery/created.yaml`. Require all replicas Ready and save each created Pod name plus its node name to pods-nodes.txt.

scenarios.title: Update a Deployment image
scenarios.stepTitle: Update an image with rolling availability
scenarios.task: Update `update-demo` from `nginx:1.27.5` to `nginx:1.28.0`. Keep four replicas; use RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1. Wait for complete replacement.

scenarios.title: Record and roll back a Deployment
scenarios.stepTitle: Inspect history and recover the broken rollout
scenarios.task: Deployment `web` is failing because its second release has an invalid image. Inspect recorded change causes and roll back to the working release. First record and complete a successful nginx:1.28.0 upgrade with change cause Successful upgrade. Then roll back to revision1, keeping four replicas of nginx:1.27.5. Save actual history to `~/book-labs/cka-06-rollout-recovery/history.txt`.

scenarios.title: Create a Pod and extract its image
scenarios.stepTitle: Create a Pod and extract only its image
scenarios.task: In `book-cka-pods`, create Ready Pod `saiyam` with image `nginx:1.28.0`. Save only the image name and newline to `~/book-labs/cka-07-pod-lifecycle/image.txt`. Use structured output instead of copying the wide table.

scenarios.title: Init container
scenarios.stepTitle: Prepare the web root with an init container
scenarios.task: Create `init-web` in `book-cka-pods`. `sam-init` using busybox:1.37.0 must complete and write `hello world` into an emptyDir mounted by nginx:1.28.0 at its web root. Verify a real HTTP response.

scenarios.title: Multi-container Pod and native sidecar
scenarios.stepTitle: Share a Pod network namespace
scenarios.task: Create Pod `multi` in `book-cka-pods` containing `web` (nginx:1.28.0) and `database` (redis:7.4.5). Both must run in the same Pod. Check Redis responds through localhost.

scenarios.title: Multi-container Pod and native sidecar
scenarios.stepTitle: Use a native sidecar for shared logs
scenarios.task: Create Pod `log-demo` in `book-cka-pods` with native sidecar `log-reader` under initContainers and restartPolicy Always. Both containers use busybox:1.37.0. A writer repeatedly appends `learning Kubernetes` to shared emptyDir `/logs/app.log`; the sidecar tails it.

scenarios.title: Multi-container shared volume
scenarios.stepTitle: Coordinate ordinary containers through a shared volume
scenarios.task: Create Pod `shared` in `book-cka-pods` with restartPolicy Never. BusyBox containers c1 and c2 write Hello from c1 container. and Hello from c2 container. to separate files in shared emptyDir /work. Container c3 waits for both files, prints both in order and exits. All three must complete successfully without a startup race.

scenarios.title: Static Pods
scenarios.stepTitle: Create a real static Pod
scenarios.task: Inspect the kubelet staticPodPath recorded in `~/book-labs/cka-08-static-pods-logs/static-dir.txt`. Place `book-cka-static.yaml` there with a Pod named `book-cka-static` in namespace `book-cka-hostpods`, image nginx:1.28.0. Let the kubelet create the mirror Pod; save its name to mirror-name.txt in the lab work directory. Do not create this Pod through kubectl apply.

scenarios.title: Static Pods
scenarios.stepTitle: Observe mirror-Pod recreation
scenarios.task: Delete only the mirror Pod for `book-cka-static`, leaving the host manifest in place. Save its UID before deletion to `~/book-labs/cka-08-static-pods-logs/mirror-before.txt`; wait for a new Ready mirror Pod with a different UID.

scenarios.title: Troubleshooting: logs
scenarios.stepTitle: Extract the correct container and previous-instance logs
scenarios.task: Save only the current logs of container `c2` in Pod `logs-demo` to `~/book-labs/cka-08-static-pods-logs/c2.txt`. Save the previous instance of `crash` container `app` to `previous.txt`. Keep the prepared Pods for verification.

scenarios.title: Highest memory consumption
scenarios.stepTitle: Find the highest memory consumer from live metrics
scenarios.task: Inspect live node and Pod metrics. Across all namespaces, save the namespace and highest memory-consuming Pod name (two space-separated fields) to highest-memory.txt in this lab’s work directory. The answer must come from current usage, not its declared resource request.

scenarios.title: Horizontal Pod autoscaling
scenarios.stepTitle: Drive a real HPA scale-out
scenarios.task: In book-cka-hpa create cpu-app Deployment using registry.k8s.io/hpa-example, initially one replica, each container requesting 200m CPU. Expose HTTP as Service cpu-app. Create an autoscaling/v2 CPU HPA with minimum1, maximum5 and 50% utilization target. Generate sustained HTTP load, wait for at least two replicas and healthy current CPU metrics, then save the live HPA JSON to hpa-scaled.json. Keep the load running for CHECK.

scenarios.title: ConfigMaps and Secrets
scenarios.stepTitle: Use ConfigMap and Secret references
scenarios.task: In `book-cka-config`, create ConfigMap `demo` with colour=green, name=saiyam, exam=cka and Secret `cka-demo`, key password, value training-only-password. Create `demo-pod` (busybox:1.37.0) importing ConfigMap keys as environment, mounting the same ConfigMap read-only at `/etc/config`, and sourcing DATABASE_PASSWORD through secretKeyRef. Tolerate book-labs.example/pool=apps:NoSchedule.

scenarios.title: ConfigMaps and Secrets
scenarios.stepTitle: Observe a mounted ConfigMap update
scenarios.task: Change only ConfigMap `demo` colour to blue. Wait until `/etc/config/colour` becomes blue in the existing Pod, while its environment variable colour remains green. Do not recreate the Pod.

scenarios.title: Probes, resource admission, and scheduling
scenarios.stepTitle: Combine probes, affinity, toleration and resource admission
scenarios.task: In `book-cka-probes`, create two-replica Deployment `web` (nginx:1.28.0), required node affinity for book-labs.example/pool=apps and matching NoSchedule toleration. Configure startup/readiness/liveness HTTP probes for `/` on named port http. Requests:100m CPU/64Mi; limits:300m CPU/128Mi. Create LimitRange `container-limits` with a per-container memory maximum of256Mi and Service `web`. Verify a512Mi Pod is rejected by admission.

scenarios.title: Probes, resource admission, and scheduling
scenarios.stepTitle: Prove failed readiness excludes an endpoint
scenarios.task: Create Pod `unready` in `book-cka-probes`, image nginx:1.28.0, with a readiness HTTP probe at `/missing` and the lab taint toleration. Expose it as Service `unready`. Its container must run but remain unready, and its endpoint must not be marked Ready. Keep the healthy web Deployment.

scenarios.title: Expose a Deployment with Services
scenarios.stepTitle: Create and test three Service types
scenarios.task: In book-cka-services expose the two web Pods with ClusterIP Service web, NodePort Service node-web using31815, and LoadBalancer Service public-web. These listen on80 and target the named http container port. Also create ClusterIP Service web-alt listening on3231 and targeting the same port80 application. Use the prepared client to test ClusterIP DNS and the node InternalIP:31815. Save loadbalancer-status.txt containing the actual external address, or Pending with a brief explanation when this VM has no load balancer implementation.

scenarios.title: NetworkPolicy
scenarios.stepTitle: Allow only the required namespace, Pod label and port
scenarios.task: Create a namespace-wide default-deny ingress policy and NetworkPolicy frontend-only in book-cka-policy. Select all Pods and allow ingress only TCP80 from Pods with role=allowed AND namespaces labelled book-labs.example/team=frontend. Prove trusted frontend traffic succeeds, while wrong-label frontend, same-label other namespace, and trusted traffic to the genuinely listening8080 port all time out.

scenarios.title: PersistentVolumeClaim and persistent data
scenarios.stepTitle: Provision a CSI volume and retain data across Pod recreation
scenarios.task: Create expandable StorageClass book-cka-expandable using local.csi.openebs.io, volgroup=book_cka_csi, storage=lvm, fsType=ext4, WaitForFirstConsumer and Delete. Create1Gi RWO claim data and BusyBox Pod app in book-cka-csi. Write persistent-csi-data to /data/marker.txt, save PVC UID and Pod UID to pvc-uid.txt and first-pod-uid.txt, delete and recreate only the Pod, and read the same data. Leave the claim bound.

scenarios.title: Resize a volume
scenarios.stepTitle: Expand the mounted ext4 filesystem without losing data
scenarios.task: Save the current mounted filesystem size (KiB) to before-kib.txt. Expand the existing data claim from1Gi to2Gi without deleting it. Wait for PVC status capacity2Gi and for the mounted ext4 filesystem to grow. Save the final claim YAML to expanded-pvc.yaml. Verify the original marker and reject a dry-run request to shrink the claim back to1Gi.

scenarios.title: Install and configure a component using Helm
scenarios.stepTitle: Install, upgrade and roll back a Helm release
scenarios.task: Render and install Jetstack cert-manager chart v1.20.4 as book-cert-manager in book-cka-cert-manager with CRDs enabled and one controller replica. Save cert-manager-rendered.yaml. Upgrade to two controller replicas with the same chart version, wait for health, then roll back to revision1. Keep the resulting three-revision history and working release.

scenarios.title: CRDs and an operator
scenarios.stepTitle: Create and diagnose custom resources
scenarios.task: Inspect the Certificate CRD schema and save its DNS-names field schema to dnsnames-schema.json. In book-cka-certificates create SelfSigned Issuer lab-selfsigned and Certificate app for DNS name app.cka.lab, writing Secret app-tls. Wait for Ready and save only the public certificate to certificate.pem. Then create Certificate missing-issuer referring to nonexistent Issuer absent, with missing-tls as its Secret. Prove reconciliation fails for that object and no Secret is issued; keep the healthy app certificate.

scenarios.title: Gateway API and HTTPRoute
scenarios.stepTitle: Create and diagnose Gateway API routes
scenarios.task: Create Gateway public-web (class lab-gateway), HTTP listener http on80 for shop.cka.lab, allowing routes in the same namespace book-cka-routing. Attach HTTPRoute shop to that listener, path prefix/, backend Service web-gateway:80. Verify current Accepted/ResolvedRefs and real HTTP. Temporarily change the backend to missing, save its ResolvedRefs=False state to unresolved-route.json, then repair it. A request using the wrong hostname must not route to the app.

scenarios.title: Ingress and TLS
scenarios.stepTitle: Expose HTTPS with a verified certificate
scenarios.task: Using prepared web.key and web.crt, create TLS Secret web-tls and Ingress web in book-cka-routing, class lab-ingress, hostname web.cka.lab, Prefix/, backend Service web-ingress:80. Use the prepared client with /trust/ca.crt to prove HTTPS succeeds with certificate verification. Prove the certificate does not match wrong.cka.lab. Keep the Gateway route working.

mappingNotes: Lab namespaces, object names and evidence paths are scoped by group to prevent collisions. Image versions are pinned patch releases.

Chapter17 shares one real CSI claim with chapter25: it starts at1Gi, survives Pod replacement with its data, then expands in place to2Gi. The container uses /data to make the persistent-filesystem checks direct.
Chapter29 uses the existing public production overlay exercise (three replicas) and adds a component overlay. This covers the same base/overlay/render/apply outcome as the book’s development overlay.
Chapter5 preserves the public reporter repair path and BusyBox image while requiring actual node labeling and scheduler selection; chapter9 uses nginx and Redis with required Pod affinity.
Local execution evidence is separate from hosted Killercoda results, which the root agent records after browser CHECKs.

validation.static: 14 JSON indexes,38 independent task/check references and263 Bash files passed syntax/reference checks.
validation.local: All14 complete local flows passed: setup, each unsolved rejection, whole solution, every check, cleanup.
validation.hosted: Recorded separately by root in browser evidence; local passes do not imply hosted passes.
validation.semanticAudit: Every assigned chapter task and its evidence outputs were compared with the final manuscript, with documented grouping adaptations.
